conviction_note: The findings sum to -1.0 and the scaled number is -1.12 (p_up 46 x abs 14). A probable revenue/EBITDA beat against a sandbagged guide ($43-44m, adj. EBITDA $1-2m) is offset by a reaction function that keys on the next-quarter guide, which has come in well below consensus three times running. A Skilling growth target that looks unreachable, a reverse split that may be announced, and Coursera's softer consumer read-through lean slightly negative. Nothing decisive and unseen by the market turned up, so p_up stays near 50 while the move size stays at the name's own ~14% median.
bar: Q3 2026 total revenue $43-44m (midpoint $43.5m), gross margin 48-49%, adj. EBITDA $1-2m, all company guidance in the Q2 release of 2026-08-06 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1364954/000136495426000085/a9901-financialresultsq220.htm). Street revenue consensus is $43.5m (Benzinga https://www.benzinga.com/quote/CHGG/earnings-forecasts) and $43.52m (MarketBeat/TheStockObserver), so two estimate sources agree with the guide midpoint. EPS consensus disagrees: -$0.07 vs -$0.09, from one analyst on Yahoo. Q4 2026 consensus could not be sourced, and that is the line the stock usually trades on.
positioning_check: MarketBeat page read 2026-11-02 (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/CHGG/short-interest/): 5.57% of float short, 9.14 days to cover, recently down 0.68%. Curved Trading/FINRA via search snippet: about 6.0m shares short at the 2026-09-30 settlement, down from 6.3m at 09-15, DTC 9.4. Moderate short interest, but high days to cover on thin $0.47m/day turnover, so some squeeze risk on a positive surprise; not a crowded short at 18-23%. No usable option chain (ATM legs not two-sided, put/call OI ratio 0.18 on 684 contracts total), so there is no skew statement. Run-up is -1.8% over 5 and 20 days; the stock is -54% from its 52-week high and +57% off its low; spot $0.707.

findings.finding: Chegg has beaten its own guide by wide margins two quarters running: Q2 2026 revenue $51.8m against a $49-50m guide and adj. EBITDA $9.1m against $5-6m; Q1 2026 revenue $63.3m against a $60-62m guide and EBITDA $15.5m against $11-12m. Repeating the Q2 pattern (+4.6% over midpoint) on the Q3 guide of $43-44m and $1-2m EBITDA points to roughly $45m revenue (+3% against the $43.5m consensus) and EBITDA of $3-5m against $1.5m. The consensus sits exactly on the guide midpoint.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats have been sold. Q2 2026 (2026-08-06) beat revenue and EBITDA and the stock fell 14.56% close to close on a weak Q3 guide. Q1 2026 (2026-05-06) beat by 3.7% on revenue and traded down 11.6% intraday on a weak Q2 guide, though the baseline closes it +10.34%. Q4 2025 (2026-02-09) closed -10.67%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at $43.5m equals the guide midpoint, so the street has not modelled the habitual beat. If the beat were priced, revenue consensus would sit around $45m and EBITDA consensus above the $2m top of the guide. It is a weak edge because the beat pattern is visible to anyone, and the stock has not paid for beats.
findings.independence: Q1 2026 beat figures from Barchart/StockStory (https://www.barchart.com/story/news/1753669/chegg-nysechgg-posts-better-than-expected-sales-in-q1-cy2026-but-stock-drops-11-6). The web-traffic finding below points the same way through a proxy.

findings.finding: Management guided Skilling (Busuu + Chegg Skills) to 'double-digit growth for the year' with a stronger second half (Q4 2025 release, 2026-02-09). H1 2026 Skilling was $35.1m ($17.6m Q1 +9%, $17.5m Q2 +2%) against $33.35m in H1 2025. A +10% full year ($76.5m) needs H2 Skilling of about $41.4m against $35.3m in H2 2025, i.e. +17%, while growth decelerated to +2% in Q2. Chegg also stopped giving segment guidance in Q2. The company's one stated growth engine is likely to show a visible miss against its own target, and the Q4 guide has come in below consensus three quarters running (Q2 guide $49.5m midpoint vs $58.6m consensus; Q3 guide $43.5m vs $48.3m; Q3 EBITDA $1.5m vs $6.0m).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: A next-quarter guide below consensus has gone with -14.56% (2026-08-06) and -10.67% (2026-02-09) close to close, and an intraday -11.6% on 2026-05-06 that closed +10.34%.
findings.why_not_priced: The street focuses on total revenue now that segment guidance has gone, and no preview found mentions the Skilling target. If it were priced, previews would treat a reset of the Skilling target as expected, and Q4 consensus would sit below the seasonal run-rate (Q4/Q3 was 0.935 in 2025). Net of the rest of the company: Academic is about 60% of revenue, and the Q3 guide implies Academic about -57% y/y against -61% in Q2. A milder Academic decline in the Q4 guide could offset a Skilling disappointment, so the size is kept small.
findings.independence: Q2 Skilling +2% from the Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1364954/000136495426000085/a9901-financialresultsq220.htm, a different document). The Coursera read-through below is a separate, independent proxy pointing the same way.

findings.finding: Chegg is out of compliance with the NYSE $1 minimum price again. The notice came 2026-07-24, the six-month cure runs to about 2027-01-24, and compliance needs a month-end close and 30-trading-day average of at least $1.00. Spot is $0.707, and stockholders approved a 1-for-4 to 1-for-15 reverse split on 2026-06-12 at the board's discretion. With roughly two month-ends left and the stock needing +41%, the board must act on the split within weeks, and an announcement alongside the Q3 release is plausible.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior reverse split. The first deficiency (December 2025) was cured by the price on 2026-06-01, and the board then said it would not proceed with a split 'at this time' (Barchart, 2026-06-17).
findings.why_not_priced: The notice is public but the timing is not. If the market had priced an imminent split, there would be pre-split selling by holders with sub-$1 or retail mandates; the stock has been flat (-1.8% over 20 days). It is probability-weighted: perhaps a one-in-three chance it lands inside the window.
findings.independence: Annual meeting 8-K with the vote approving the 1:4 to 1:15 range (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1364954/000136495426000066/chgg-20260612.htm).

findings.finding: Third-party web traffic for Chegg (AltIndex, aggregated estimates) reads 3.32m visits in July, 3.26m in August and 4.93m in September 2026 (+51% m/m back-to-school). The Q3 average of 3.84m is down about 13% q/q from Q2's 4.40m (6.11m/3.94m/3.14m), against the roughly -24% q/q in Academic revenue implied by the Q3 guide ($43.5m less about $17.7m Skilling against Q2 Academic $34.3m).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Same reported-quarter line as the first finding; beats have been sold (see above).
findings.why_not_priced: It is an obscure aggregator series, and no preview cites it. It is a proxy only: a modelled estimate, with no year-ago September on the same provider (Semrush's October 2025 figure of 11.59m is a different model and not comparable), and subscription revenue lags traffic. If it were priced, consensus would sit above the guide midpoint.
findings.independence: Shares direction with the first finding's beat pattern but rests on a different source. Proxy only.

findings.finding: Coursera, which reported after Chegg last spoke (2026-10-29), said Q3 consumer revenue fell 9% y/y on a normalized basis, that leading funnel indicators softened, and that it expects further consumer deceleration in Q4 and a low-double-digit consumer decline in 2027. This is a read-through to Chegg Skilling's consumer upskilling and language (Busuu) demand.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no direct history of Chegg reacting to peer prints; its guide line has been the mover (see the Skilling finding).
findings.why_not_priced: It is a peer print after Chegg's last guide, so consensus may not have moved, and Chegg's Skilling estimates are thin (one analyst on Yahoo). It is a proxy: Coursera's consumer business is mostly courses and certificates, not language learning, so the transmission is unconfirmed.
findings.independence: The consumer -9% figure comes from the MarketBeat call summary (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/transcript-coursera-q3-earnings-call-highlights-2026-10-29/). It points the same way as the Skilling finding but is a separate entity.

findings.finding: Chegg repaid the last $33.9m of its 0% convertible notes at maturity on 2026-09-01 and is debt-free, with about $38m of pro forma cash (June 30 cash of $72.3m less the repayment) against a market cap of about $78m. $120.7m remains on the buyback authorization, which was used for only $1.7m in Q2. With financing risk removed, a resumed or larger buyback, or a cash-floor narrative, is possible at the print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed reaction to buyback news in the baseline window.
findings.why_not_priced: The repayment is public, so this is mostly priced. What is not priced is any capital-return decision, and EV of about $40m against cash-burn risk (Q3 EBITDA guide $1-2m, capex about $3-4m a quarter) makes a large buyback less likely than a small one. The financing question was asked: the money retired debt, with no new financing, so it is neutral to slightly positive.
findings.independence: Q2 release confirms the $120.7m authorization and $1.7m repurchased (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1364954/000136495426000085/a9901-financialresultsq220.htm).

findings.finding: Judge Mehta (D.D.C.) dismissed Chegg's antitrust suit against Google over AI Overviews on 2026-09-30. A litigation upside option that management had pointed to as a cause of the traffic collapse is gone, and the call may address an appeal or the costs.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No baseline print was tied to this line.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it is public a month before the print and the stock barely moved. Only commentary on an appeal at the call is new.
findings.independence: Same ruling reported by letsdatascience (https://letsdatascience.com/news/judge-dismisses-chegg-and-penske-ai-overviews-antitrust-laws-39a53d81); one fact, counted once.

outside_window.finding: The NYSE cure deadline for the $1 minimum price is about 2027-01-24, with the last month-end tests at 2026-11-30 and 2026-12-31. Failure triggers suspension and delisting procedures if no reverse split is effected.

searched_and_found_nothing: EDGAR filings since 2026-08-06 (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001364954): only the 2026-09-01 debt-repayment 8-K and Forms 4. All Forms 4 (Rosensweig 2026-09-12 and 2026-10-28, Longo 2026-10-12) are code F tax withholding on RSU vesting. No open-market insider buying or selling, and no new 8-K item 1.01/5.02/2.05.
No Chegg press release between 2026-09-01 and the 2026-10-13 date announcement. The date announcement moved from BusinessWire to GlobeNewswire, which is only cost-cutting colour.
No AI-data-licensing customer or deal terms announced since the 2026-05-13 'AI model training' release.
No sale or divestiture of Busuu or Chegg Skills found in 2026.

Q2 2026 call transcript (fool.com 404, benzinga 403, stocktaper 429 from the site, not a tool budget limit). Only the prepared-remarks content in the 8-K and secondary summaries were read.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with (unusable chain), and the run-up is flat at -1.8%. The slight negative lean agrees with the reaction history (5 of 8 prints down, guide-driven sell-offs), while the moderate short interest and 9 days to cover on a $78m name with about $38m of net cash argue that the downside is not free; both push p_up toward 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a reaction; this name sells beats): reported-quarter beat finding cut from +1.0 to +0.5.

Lesson 9 (size a segment finding net of the rest): the Skilling-target guidance finding cut from -1.5 to -1.0, because the Q3 guide implies a milder Academic decline (-57% vs -61% y/y) that could offset it.
Lesson 5 (proxies are small): web-traffic proxy cut from +0.5 to +0.3 and the Coursera read-through from -0.5 to -0.4; both kept as filed.

Lesson 8 (thin coverage, understatement): abs_move_pct raised from 13 to 14 (one-analyst name, median own reaction 13.6%); p_up moved from 45 to 46 after the lesson-7 positioning check (9 days to cover).

Lesson 6: bar verified against the company guide plus two agreeing revenue estimates, so no cap is needed. The NYSE cure deadline is placed in outside_window; only the in-window chance of a split announcement stays in findings.
Left standing: the reverse-split, buyback and Google-dismissal findings.
